Header:

Recording: yes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood), Lina Gomez (Redwood), Ravi Menon (Redwood), Dr. Maya Chen (Aurelia), Evan Brooks (Aurelia), Sara Park (Aurelia), Omar Ruiz (Aurelia)

AUTO SUMMARY (auto):
- Weekly POC sync focused on TTFT (first token fast) improvements, streaming behaviour, sequence length distributions, and kernel choices for quantized models.
- Agreement to run A/B kernel experiments, share prompt traces, and produce cost/latency projections.

TOPICS (auto):
1) TTFT optimizations and warm-KV strategies
2) Streaming chunking and early-flush behavior
3) Kernel selection and quant profiles
4) Pilot success metrics and next steps

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Samir: hey everybody, thanks for joining, um quick roll call. we got, uh, team here from Aurelia, welcome.
[00:11] Dr. Maya: thanks Samir, morning all. excited to see the TTFT numbers.
[00:16] Lina: quick agenda — recap last week's tuning, go over new kernel A/B plan, then streaming quirks we saw with short prompts.
[00:28] Evan: sounds good. just a note — we pulled more prompt traces overnight, the distribution shifted a bit toward shorter sequences which I think matters for TTFT.
[00:39] Ravi: great, okay let's dive. Samir, do you want to start with the latest first token numbers?
[00:45] Samir: sure, um so baseline from last week — hosted default kernel on g5-like instance gave us median first-token at about 145ms with cold KV, with warm KV we saw 42 to 50ms depending on batch structure. but important caveat, those were with a 512-seq baseline not the actual mix.
[01:06] Evan: right and our user flows are mostly 32 to 128 tokens often, very few 512s. maybe 5% above 256.
[01:15] Lina: that's key — kernel selection and micro-ops change when sequence length is lower. some kernels are optimized for long sequences and they actually add overhead on short ones, so we want to prioritize short-seq kernels for your workload.
[01:30] Dr. Maya: can you explain the warm-KV story? we saw inconsistent gains across runs.
[01:36] Lina: yeah, warm KV depends on prefix caching and how the request routing touches the same worker. if there are many tiny requests spread across pods you lose KV locality. we've suggested session-pinning and sticky routing in the config — that gave the 42ms number in our lab.
[01:53] Evan: sticky routing — that affects concurrency though? we worry about utilization.
[01:58] Ravi: correct tradeoff — sticky increases per-worker hotness which can reduce batch sizes but improve TTFT. we can simulate both; that's part of the A/B.
[02:08] [crosstalk, inaudible]
[02:15] Omar: from product side, for end-users a 40ms vs 150ms first token is huge, but cost uplift needs to be clear.
[02:23] Samir: agreed. we'll include unit cost delta in the projection.
[02:27] Lina: next, kernel A/B plan: we have 4 kernel builds to test — baseline, seq-optimized, quant-friendly, and hybrid small-seq fastpath. the idea is to run identical request traces with session-pinning and without, warm and cold cache, then measure TTFT, p95 generation latency and token cost.
[02:45] Evan: can we also toggle streaming chunk sizes? we noticed for short answers the stream terminates late — UI shows a pause.
[02:54] Lina: yes, streaming chunk config is separate. currently our runtime flushes every 64 tokens or when buffer crosses 40ms, but for short outputs that's too coarse. we can lower flush threshold for your pilot to 8 tokens / 15ms early-chunk flush. caveat: more network packets.
[03:14] Sara: any impact on costs or infra? more flushes = more latency overhead?
[03:19] Ravi: CPU overhead at the transport layer rises slightly; network egress may go up but token compute cost is same. We'll quantify in tests.
[03:27] Dr. Maya: what about quantization choices — we have regulatory concerns about deterministic behavior and hallucination drift.
[03:34] Lina: good point. quant profiles we recommend: 8-bit symmetric for most, with 4-bit for non-critical workloads. for hallucination/regression risk we tie quality evals to your prompt set and run a BLEU-like or exact-match set of checks. if we see drift we rollback kernel/quant combo.
[03:51] Evan: can we pin a canary with fallback? like if quality score drops below threshold auto-fallback to baseline kernel.
[03:57] Samir: yes, rollout policies support canary + auto rollback, we can do a 5% canary for 24h then expand.
[04:04] Omar: on private deployment, is the kernel binary different or just config? we plan to run in our VPC with KMS.
[04:12] Lina: kernel builds are the same binary family but compiled with different code paths and instructions for the CPU/GPU. for private deployment we push the exact same kernels; we just need to ensure CUDA / driver compatibility. KMS is supported, and audit logs will be in the control plane you host.
[04:27] Sara: speaking of logs — retention and PII — we need to ensure prompt traces are redacted before leaving cluster.
[04:33] Samir: agreed, we can provide an agent that scrubs PII fields and hashes identifiers before upload. Evan, you flagged providing traces?
[04:40] Evan: yes, we'll extract and anonymize. may be a small mismatch in tokenization but it's fine.
[04:46] Lina: demo of quick benchmark plan — we propose two runs: run A = sticky routing + small-seq kernel + flushing 8 tokens; run B = non-sticky routing + hybrid kernel + default flush. collect TTFT, p95, token cost, and sample quality checks per prompt.
[05:03] Dr. Maya: timeline?
[05:05] Samir: we can provision tests in 24–48 hours. results back by next Wed. Lina will own harness.
[05:12] Evan: please include costs at 100k qps-equivalent and 1M monthly tokens — easier for finance.
[05:19] Ravi: small ask — please also run a long-tail test with synthetic 512 sequences to ensure no regressions for the small set of long requests.
[05:26] Samir: yes, we will.
[05:28] [silence 5s]
[05:33] Omar: one surprise we had — sometimes streaming output duplicates the last token on reconnection. is that a known thing?
[05:39] Lina: that's an ordering edge case with our chunk-reassembly logic when the client reconnects mid-stream; we've patched it in nightly but not in stable. we can backport the patch to the pilot image.
[05:50] Sara: great, please do.
[05:53] Dr. Maya: security review item — will you share SOC2 artifacts and network diagrams?
[05:58] Samir: yes, we'll share SOC2 summary and private deployment checklist. we'll also include audit log samples and KMS architecture notes.
[06:07] Evans: (sic) Evan: small nit — in the last run we saw worker pre-emption spikes, maybe due to autoscaler config. can you pin min replicas?
[06:15] Ravi: yes we can enforce min replicas and reserved capacity in Dedicated. for hosted pilot we can also reserve capacity.
[06:22] Dr. Maya: okay, recap and owners?
[06:25] Samir: recap: Redwood runs A/B kernels across warm/cold KV and streaming flush settings; customer shares prompt traces and validates redaction; Redwood produces cost/latency spreadsheet and pushes patch for streaming duplication; plan to reconvene after results next Wed.
[06:41] Omar: thanks all.
[06:43] Samir: thanks — we'll follow up in email with links to the test harness and the spreadsheet.
